config.title: Build typed form library core APIs

intro.title: Build typed form library core APIs
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build the core APIs for a simple, typed form library in TypeScript. You will learn how to use TypeScript's generic types to create a form structure that is type-safe, ensuring your form data and validation are predictable. The main constructs involved are generic functions, interfaces, and type parameters. By the end, you'll have a foundational library that can manage form state and validation with full TypeScript support.
intro.usecase: Typed form libraries are essential in enterprise applications where data validation and type safety are critical. You'll find them in complex form-heavy interfaces like insurance claim systems, financial dashboards, and healthcare patient portals where each field must match specific data types and validation rules. These typed APIs prevent runtime errors in e-commerce checkout flows, user registration forms, and admin panels by catching type mismatches during development. As a developer, you'll use typed form libraries to ensure data consistency, reduce bugs, and improve maintainability in any application collecting structured user input.

objectives: Construct a typed form state object with TypeScript interfaces
Implement validation functions that enforce type constraints on form fields
Configure a form handler to manage user input and state updates
Bind form controls to typed state properties with proper event handling
Initialize form values with default data while maintaining type safety
Manipulate form state through controlled input components
Integrate validation logic into form submission workflows

steps.title: Import TypeScript types and utilities
steps.instruction: Import the TypeScript types and utilities needed for building typed form APIs. Import the following: 'FormData', 'FormErrors', 'ValidationRule', and 'createForm' from './form-types'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the named exports from the './form-types' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple named exports
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// Import the required types and utilities from './form-types'

steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, making the types and utilities available for use in the form library.
successCriteria: FormData, FormErrors, ValidationRule, and createForm are imported from './form-types'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required items, but not all. Make sure to import FormData, FormErrors, ValidationRule, and createForm from './form-types'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import FormData, FormErrors, ValidationRule, and createForm from './form-types'.

steps.title: Define the FormField interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named FormField with three properties: name (string), value (unknown), and validation (optional boolean).
steps.hint: Use the interface keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a FormField interface that can be used to type form field configurations.
successCriteria: The FormField interface is defined with name: string, value: unknown, and validation?: boolean properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your interface has all three required properties with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Remember to create an interface named FormField with the specified properties.

steps.title: Create the FormState type
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript type called FormState that represents a collection of FormField objects.
steps.hint: Think of FormState as an object where each key is a string (field name) and each value is a FormField.
steps.expectedOutcome: A FormState type is defined, ready to be used as the main form data structure.
successCriteria: FormState type is defined with an index signature mapping string keys to FormField values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure FormState uses an index signature with string keys and FormField values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The FormState type isn't defined correctly. It should be a type with string keys mapping to FormField objects.

steps.title: Define the ValidationResult type
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript type called ValidationResult with two properties: isValid (boolean) and errorMessage (string).
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword to create a type alias. Add the properties with their respective TypeScript types.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ValidationResult type is defined with the correct property types.
successCriteria: ValidationResult type exists with isValid: boolean and errorMessage: string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure ValidationResult has both isValid (boolean) and errorMessage (string) properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ValidationResult type definition is missing or incorrect. It should have isValid: boolean and errorMessage: string properties.

steps.title: Create the createFormField function
steps.instruction: Create a function named createFormField that returns a properly typed FormField object.
steps.hint: Define a function that takes the necessary parameters to construct a FormField and returns an object matching the FormField interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: A createFormField function is defined and ready to be used to create typed form field objects.
successCriteria: The createFormField function exists and returns a FormField object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function returns a properly typed FormField object. Check the interface definition from earlier steps.
steps.feedbackWrong: The createFormField function is missing or doesn't return a FormField object. Review the FormField interface and create a function that constructs an object matching that type.

steps.title: Implement the updateFieldValue function
steps.instruction: Create a function named updateFieldValue that takes a FormState, a field name, and a new value, and returns a new FormState with that field's value updated.
steps.hint: The function should accept three parameters: the current form state, the field name (string), and the new value (any). It should return a new FormState object with the updated field value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a function that can update a specific field's value in the form state while preserving type safety.
successCriteria: The updateFieldValue function is defined with proper TypeScript parameters and returns a new FormState object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function accepts all three parameters and returns a new FormState object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't match the expected signature. It should take FormState, a field name, and a value, then return a new FormState.

steps.title: Create the validateField function
steps.instruction: Create a function called validateField that takes a FormField parameter and returns a ValidationResult. Inside, check if the field's value is empty and return an appropriate ValidationResult.
steps.hint: The function should have the signature (field: FormField): ValidationResult. Use the field's value property to determine if it's empty.
steps.expectedOutcome: A validateField function that validates a form field and returns a ValidationResult object.
successCriteria: The validateField function is defined with proper TypeScript typing and returns a ValidationResult.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function takes a FormField parameter and returns a ValidationResult.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validateField function is not properly defined. Check the function signature and return type.

steps.title: Implement the validateForm function
steps.instruction: Create a function named validateForm that takes a FormState object as a parameter and returns a boolean indicating whether all fields in the form are valid.
steps.hint: You'll need to iterate through the fields in the FormState, check each field's isValid property, and return true only if all fields are valid.
steps.expectedOutcome: A validateForm function that properly checks all fields' validity and returns the overall form validity status.
successCriteria: The validateForm function exists, accepts a FormState parameter, iterates through fields, checks isValid properties, and returns a boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function accepts a FormState parameter and returns true only when all fields are valid.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validateForm function isn't implemented correctly. It should take FormState, check all field validities, and return a boolean.

steps.title: Create the getFormValues function
steps.instruction: Create a function called getFormValues that takes a FormState object as a parameter and returns an object containing all field values from the form state.
steps.hint: The function should iterate through the fields in the form state and collect their values into a new object.
steps.expectedOutcome: A getFormValues function that extracts all field values from the form state in a type-safe manner.
successCriteria: The getFormValues function is defined, takes a FormState parameter, and returns an object with field values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function properly extracts all field values from the FormState.
steps.feedbackWrong: The getFormValues function is missing or doesn't correctly extract field values from the form state.

steps.title: Implement the createForm function
steps.instruction: Create a function named createForm that takes an array of FormField objects as its parameter and returns a FormApi object. Inside the function, initialize a form state object using the provided fields.
steps.hint: The function should accept fields as a parameter, create an initial FormState using those fields, and return an object that matches the FormApi interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createForm function is defined with proper TypeScript typing and returns a FormApi object with placeholder implementations for its methods.
successCriteria: The createForm function exists, accepts FormField[] as parameter, initializes a FormState object, and returns an object matching the FormApi interface structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function accepts FormField[] as a parameter and returns an object with all the methods defined in the FormApi interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The createForm function should initialize form state and return a FormApi object. Check that you're using the correct types and structure.

steps.title: Export all form library APIs
steps.instruction: Export all the types, interfaces, and functions you've created in this lesson using named exports.
steps.hint: Add export statements before each type, interface, and function definition to make them available for import in other files.
steps.expectedOutcome: All form library APIs (types, interfaces, functions) will be properly exported and ready for use in other TypeScript modules.
successCriteria: FormField, FormState, ValidationResult, createFormField, updateFieldValue, validateField, validateForm, getFormValues, FormApi, and createForm are all exported using named exports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported some items, but not all required APIs. Make sure to export FormField, FormState, ValidationResult, createFormField, updateFieldValue, validateField, validateForm, getFormValues, FormApi, and createForm.
steps.feedbackWrong: No exports were found. Remember to add export statements for all the types, interfaces, and functions you've created in this lesson.
